question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I wish we had ______ come here.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. never.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "I wish + had + V3 (past perfect)" expresses a regret about a past action. The speaker regrets having come to this place, so the negative adverb "never" fits perfectly.

◦ Correct: I wish we had never come here. (काश हम यहाँ कभी न आए होते)

• "Never" is placed between the auxiliary "had" and the past participle "come" — the standard position for a mid-sentence adverb of frequency.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "right" — "had right come" is ungrammatical; "right" is not an adverb of negation.

• Option 2 "clear" — "had clear come" is meaningless.

• Option 4 "agreed" — "had agreed come" is wrong; it would need "had agreed to come".

NOTE

• Uses of "wish":

◦ Wish + past simple → regret about the present (I wish I knew the answer).

◦ Wish + past perfect → regret about the past (I wish we had never come here).

◦ Wish + would → irritation / desire for change (I wish you would stop shouting).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Carnal
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Spiritual.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Carnal" means relating to the body and its physical/sensual desires; fleshly, worldly. (शारीरिक / दैहिक)

◦ Example: The saint warned his disciples against carnal pleasures.

• Its direct antonym is "Spiritual", meaning relating to the soul or spirit rather than the body. (आध्यात्मिक)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Material" (relating to physical things/matter) is closer to a synonym of carnal than an antonym.

• Option 3 "Temporal" means worldly/secular or relating to time — again worldly, not spiritual.

• Option 4 "Somatic" means of the body — an exact synonym of carnal, hence the opposite of what is required.

NOTE

• Synonyms of carnal: fleshly, sensual, bodily, physical, somatic, worldly.

• Antonyms of carnal: spiritual, chaste, moral, pure, ascetic.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Fail to function normally
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Malfunction.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Malfunction" means to fail to work or function in the normal or correct way. (ठीक से काम न करना / खराबी)

◦ Example: The engine began to malfunction halfway through the journey.

• The prefix "mal-" means bad/wrong, and "function" means to work — so mal + function = to work badly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Maltreat" = to treat someone cruelly or badly (दुर्व्यवहार करना).

• Option 2 "Mangle" = to damage something by crushing or tearing it badly.

• Option 3 "Manipulate" = to control or influence cleverly, often unfairly.

NOTE

• Common "mal-" words: malnutrition (bad nourishment), malpractice (wrong professional conduct), malicious (spiteful), malady (a disease), maladroit (clumsy).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given phrase.

All of a sudden
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Quickly and unexpectedly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "all of a sudden" means very quickly and without any warning; suddenly and unexpectedly. (अचानक / एकाएक)

◦ Example: All of a sudden, the lights went out and the hall fell silent.

• The key idea in the phrase is the element of surprise — the event was not anticipated.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Intentionally" (deliberately) is the opposite idea — a sudden event is not planned.

• Option 3 "Quickly and Expectedly" contradicts the phrase, because "sudden" implies the event was not expected.

• Option 4 "Accidently" (a misspelling of "accidentally") means by chance, which is not the same as suddenly.

NOTE

• Similar expressions: "out of the blue", "in the blink of an eye", "without warning", "on a sudden impulse".

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

My daughter was / invited to lunch / hosted by the Governor / at his residence.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. invited to lunch.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Names of meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner) normally take no article — "We had lunch at two."

• But when the meal is particularised/qualified by a describing phrase or clause, the indefinite article "a" is required. Here "lunch" is qualified by "hosted by the Governor", so it must be "invited to a lunch".

◦ Correct: My daughter was invited to a lunch hosted by the Governor at his residence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Segment 1 "My daughter was" is a correct subject + verb (passive) opening.

• Segment 3 "hosted by the Governor" is a correct past-participle phrase modifying "lunch".

• Segment 4 "at his residence" uses the correct preposition "at" for a place.

NOTE

• Compare: "We had dinner at eight." (no article) vs "We attended a dinner given in his honour." (qualified — article needed). The same rule applies to "a lunch hosted by...", "a breakfast arranged by...".

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Rectifie.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Rectifie" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Rectify", which means to put something right; to correct an error. (सुधारना / ठीक करना)

◦ Example: The bank promised to rectify the mistake in my statement.

• Spelling key: REC + TI + FY — the word ends in "-fy", not "-fie".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Resist" (to oppose or withstand), "Recruit" (to enrol new members/soldiers) and "Repulse" (to drive back; to repel) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Verbs ending in "-fy": rectify, classify, justify, notify, magnify, satisfy. The "-ie" spelling appears only in the past form: rectify → rectified, and in the noun rectification.

question:
Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The maintenence department did a fabulous job.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. maintenance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling of the underlined word is "maintenance", meaning the process of keeping something in good condition/repair. (रख-रखाव)

◦ Correct: The maintenance department did a fabulous job.

• Spelling key: MAIN + TEN + ANCE. Note that although the verb is "maintain", the noun drops the "i" and ends in "-ance", not "-ence".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "mainteanance", Option 3 "maintenannce" (double "n") and Option 4 "meintenance" are all wrong spellings.

• The printed form "maintenence" is wrong because it uses "-ence" instead of "-ance".

NOTE

• Similar tricky "-ance" nouns: appearance, performance, resistance, acceptance, attendance. Compare with "-ence" nouns: existence, occurrence, persistence, independence.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word in the following sentence to fill in the blank.

The novel’s intricate plot and rich character development kept readers ________(committed) from the beginning to the end.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. engaged.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The bracketed word "committed" here means fully involved/absorbed and devoted to something. Its closest synonym in this context is "engaged", meaning deeply involved and holding one's interest and attention. (तल्लीन / जुड़ा हुआ)

◦ Correct: The novel's intricate plot and rich character development kept readers engaged from the beginning to the end.

• The context words "intricate plot" and "rich character development" show that the readers' interest was held throughout — exactly what "engaged" conveys.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "secluded" (kept away/isolated from others) is unrelated to interest.

• Option 3 "detached" (aloof, uninvolved) is the antonym of the required sense.

• Option 4 "dismantled" (taken apart, pulled to pieces) is used for machines/structures, not readers.

NOTE

• Synonyms of engaged (in this sense): absorbed, engrossed, involved, occupied, immersed, riveted. Antonyms: detached, uninterested, indifferent, aloof.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

These things are very hard to swallow.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. difficult to believe.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "hard to swallow" means difficult to believe or accept. It is used for statements, excuses or news that seem unconvincing or unpleasant. (विश्वास करने में कठिन)

◦ Example: His story about missing the flight twice was a bit hard to swallow.

• Here the sense is figurative, not literal — it has nothing to do with actually swallowing food.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "difficult to eat" is the literal meaning and is therefore the trap option in an idiom question.

• Option 1 "difficult to resist" and Option 2 "difficult to speak" do not match the idiom at all.

NOTE

• Related idioms: "a bitter pill to swallow" (an unpleasant fact one must accept), "take it with a pinch of salt" (not to believe something completely), "swallow one's pride" (to accept humiliation).

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

The decision to go on a trip after my vacations was the ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. icing on the cake.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "the icing on the cake" means an extra benefit that makes a good situation even better. (सोने पे सुहागा)

◦ Correct: The decision to go on a trip after my vacations was the icing on the cake.

• "Icing" is the sweet layer spread over a cake — the cake is already good, and the icing makes it better; hence the figurative meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "ice on the cake", 3 "apple on the cake" and 4 "icing on the brownie" are distorted forms and are not accepted idioms. Idioms must be used in their fixed, unchanged form.

NOTE

• Similar idioms: "cherry on top" (an added bonus), "the best of both worlds", "a blessing in disguise". Opposite idea: "to add insult to injury" (to make a bad situation worse).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The new software / consists from / several features / and tools.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. consists from.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "consist" is always followed by the preposition "of" when it means "to be made up of". "Consists from" is incorrect.

◦ Correct: The new software consists of several features and tools.

• Note also that "consist" is a stative verb — it is not normally used in the continuous form ("is consisting of" is wrong).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Segment 2 "several features" and Segment 4 "and tools" are correct plural noun phrases.

• Segment 3 "The new software" is correct — "software" is an uncountable noun (never "softwares").

NOTE

• Fixed verb + preposition combinations: consist of, comprise (no preposition), composed of, made up of, depend on, insist on, deprive of, accuse of. Remember: "comprise" is never followed by "of" — "The team comprises ten players.".

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

It's easy to say that you'll start exercising every day, but it is ______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. easier said than done.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "easier said than done" means much more difficult to do in practice than it sounds in words. (कहना आसान, करना मुश्किल)

◦ Correct: It's easy to say that you'll start exercising every day, but it is easier said than done.

• The sentence itself gives the clue: "It's easy to say ... but ..." — a clear contrast between speaking and doing.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "like a fish out of water" = feeling uncomfortable in unfamiliar surroundings.

• Option 3 "crying wolf" = raising a false alarm repeatedly so that no one believes you later.

• Option 4 "going the extra mile" = making a special effort beyond what is expected.

NOTE

• The conjunction "but" signals a contrast, so the missing idiom must oppose "easy to say" — only "easier said than done" does that.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Paralycis.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Paralycis" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Paralysis", meaning the loss of the ability to move (and sometimes to feel) in part or most of the body. (लकवा / पक्षाघात)

◦ Example: The accident left him with partial paralysis of the legs.

• Spelling key: PARA + LY + SIS — the ending is "-sis", not "-cis".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Lyricist" (a writer of song lyrics), "Indigestion" (difficulty in digesting food) and "Patron" (a supporter/benefactor) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Medical nouns ending in "-sis": paralysis, diagnosis, analysis, thrombosis, tuberculosis. Their plurals change "-sis" to "-ses": paralyses, analyses, diagnoses. The related adjective is "paralytic" and the verb is "paralyse/paralyze".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.

Uncle Joe is ___________________(reputable) for spending 10 years of his youth in prison due to armed robbery.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. notorious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Reputable" means having a good reputation; respected and trustworthy. (प्रतिष्ठित)

• Its antonym is "notorious", meaning famous for something bad — infamous. Since Uncle Joe spent ten years in prison for armed robbery, he is famous for a bad reason. (कुख्यात)

◦ Correct: Uncle Joe is notorious for spending 10 years of his youth in prison due to armed robbery.

• The collocation "notorious for + (bad deed)" is also grammatically perfect here.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "mournful" (very sad/sorrowful) and Option 2 "anxious" (worried) describe feelings, not reputation.

• Option 3 "well-known" is neutral/positive in tone and is closer to a synonym of reputable, so it cannot be the antonym.

NOTE

• Note the difference: famous (well known for something good) vs notorious/infamous (well known for something bad). Antonyms of reputable: notorious, infamous, disreputable, discreditable, shady.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

If you work hard, you secure good marks.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. you secure.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• This is a Conditional Type 1 sentence (a real/probable future condition). Its correct structure is:

◦ If + Subject + V1 (present simple), Subject + will + V1

• The "if-clause" here is "If you work hard" (present simple), so the main clause must use "will secure", not the present simple "secure".

◦ Correct: If you work hard, you will secure good marks.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "If you" and "work hard" correctly form the conditional clause in the present simple.

• "good marks" is a correct object phrase.

• Remember the golden rule: never use "will" in the "if" clause of a Type 1 conditional.

NOTE

• The three main conditionals:

◦ Type 1 (real future): If it rains, we will cancel the match.

◦ Type 2 (unreal present): If it rained, we would cancel the match.

◦ Type 3 (unreal past): If it had rained, we would have cancelled the match.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A person who is skilled in making maps
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Cartographer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Cartographer" is a person who is skilled in drawing or making maps and charts. (मानचित्रकार)

◦ Example: The cartographer spent months mapping the coastline.

• The study/art of map-making is called "cartography" (from the French "carte" = map).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Calligrapher" = a person skilled in beautiful handwriting (calligraphy).

• Option 2 "Curator" = a person in charge of a museum or its collection.

• Option 3 "Cacographer" = a person with bad handwriting or bad spelling (the opposite of a calligrapher).

NOTE

• Other useful one-word substitutes: Geographer (one who studies the earth's surface), Cosmographer (one who maps the universe), Topographer (one who describes the physical features of a place), Philatelist (a stamp collector), Numismatist (a coin collector).

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words.

Sita loves her glass container in which she has many fish.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. aquarium.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "aquarium" is a glass tank/container filled with water in which fish and other water creatures are kept. (मछलीघर)

◦ Correct: Sita loves her aquarium.

• The word comes from the Latin "aqua" meaning water.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "cannister (canister)" = a small metal or plastic container for tea, flour, gas, etc. — not for fish.

• Option 3 "planetarium" = a building/room where images of stars and planets are projected on a dome.

• Option 4 "museum" = a building where objects of historical, artistic or scientific interest are displayed.

NOTE

• Related "-arium/-orium" words: aquarium (water animals), vivarium (living animals), terrarium (small land plants/animals), herbarium (dried plants), sanatorium (a place for recovering patients), auditorium (a hall for an audience).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can rectify the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to rectify it, select ‘no rectification needed’.

His claim to be the smartly kid in the school was a bit hyperbole!
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. smartest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Smartly" is an adverb, but the blank comes before the noun "kid", where an adjective is required. So the adverb must be replaced.

• The definite article "the" before the slot and the phrase "in the school" (comparison within a whole group) demand the superlative degree — "the smartest".

◦ Correct: His claim to be the smartest kid in the school was a bit hyperbole!

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "no rectification needed" is wrong because an adverb cannot modify the noun "kid".

• Option 3 "smarter" is the comparative and would need "than" (smarter than the others), not "the ... in the school".

• Option 4 "smart" (positive degree) does not suit "the ... in the school", which calls for a superlative.

NOTE

• Degrees of comparison: smart – smarter (than) – the smartest (in/of). Use the superlative with "the" when one member is compared with all others in a group: "the tallest boy in the class", "the best player in the team".

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Easily set on fire
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Inflammable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Inflammable" means easily set on fire; capable of burning quickly. (शीघ्र ज्वलनशील)

◦ Example: Petrol is highly inflammable, so smoking is banned near fuel pumps.

• Important: "inflammable" and "flammable" mean the same thing. Here "in-" comes from "inflame" (to set on fire) and is not a negative prefix. The true opposite is "non-inflammable".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Innocuous" = harmless, causing no injury or offence.

• Option 2 "Ingrained" = deeply fixed/firmly established (ingrained habits).

• Option 4 "Inimical" = hostile, unfriendly, harmful to something.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: combustible (able to catch fire), incombustible / fireproof (unable to burn), volatile (evaporating rapidly), explosive (liable to blow up).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

She has / bought / a car / two years ago.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. She has.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adverbial "two years ago" refers to a definite/finished point in the past, so the sentence must be in the Simple Past tense, not the Present Perfect.

• The Present Perfect ("has bought") can never be used with a definite past-time expression such as "ago", "yesterday", "last year" or "in 2019". Hence the faulty segment is "She has".

◦ Correct: She bought a car two years ago.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Segment 2 "bought" is the correct past form / past participle of "buy" (buy – bought – bought) and stays unchanged.

• Segment 3 "a car" is a correct singular countable noun phrase.

• Segment 4 "two years ago" is a correct adverbial of past time.

NOTE

• Present Perfect goes with indefinite time markers: already, just, yet, ever, never, recently, so far, since, for.

• Simple Past goes with definite past markers: ago, yesterday, last night, in 1947, then.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Students put their heart and soul into studies while (1)________ for examinations. They prepare the syllabus by giving many revisions, making important points on flash cards, preparing notes throughout the year. They read reference books in order to score good marks in the examination. This is the demanding (2)________ of all the students who are appearing in the examinations. But, most students feel tensed on the day before an examination. Everyone is in a state of (3)________ as to what questions would be asked in the paper and whether they could write their answers properly to get good marks. Such overthinking is the cause of (4)________ which definitely affects their performance. They should revise the subject regularly and should not keep their doubts pending. This will not create a (5)________ of backlog and they will get sufficient time to resolve their problem.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. preparing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank follows the preposition-like conjunction "while" and precedes "for examinations". The fixed collocation is "to prepare for an examination" — to get ready for it by studying. (परीक्षा की तैयारी करना)

◦ Correct: Students put their heart and soul into studies while preparing for examinations.

• The very next sentence ("They prepare the syllabus by giving many revisions ... preparing notes") confirms that the passage is about preparation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "calculating" (working out by mathematics) does not collocate with "for examinations".

• Option 2 "guiding" (showing the way) would need an object — one guides somebody.

• Option 3 "producing" (manufacturing/creating) is entirely out of context.

NOTE

• Useful collocations: prepare for an exam, appear for/in an exam, sit for an exam, revise for an exam, score/secure marks, clear/crack an exam.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Students put their heart and soul into studies while (1)________ for examinations. They prepare the syllabus by giving many revisions, making important points on flash cards, preparing notes throughout the year. They read reference books in order to score good marks in the examination. This is the demanding (2)________ of all the students who are appearing in the examinations. But, most students feel tensed on the day before an examination. Everyone is in a state of (3)________ as to what questions would be asked in the paper and whether they could write their answers properly to get good marks. Such overthinking is the cause of (4)________ which definitely affects their performance. They should revise the subject regularly and should not keep their doubts pending. This will not create a (5)________ of backlog and they will get sufficient time to resolve their problem.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. routine.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "routine" is a regular, fixed way of doing things — a set daily schedule of activities. (दिनचर्या)

• The preceding lines describe activities repeated throughout the year (revisions, flash cards, notes, reference books). Such a repeated pattern of study is exactly a demanding routine.

◦ Correct: This is the demanding routine of all the students who are appearing in the examinations.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "principle" = a basic rule or belief — not a set of daily activities.

• Option 2 "method" = a particular way/procedure of doing one thing; it does not carry the sense of a regularly repeated schedule.

• Option 4 "habit" = an individual's automatic personal tendency; "the demanding habit of all the students" does not fit the description of a planned study schedule.

NOTE

• "Routine" collocates well with daily, strict, demanding, gruelling, fixed — e.g., "a gruelling training routine", "his daily routine".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Students put their heart and soul into studies while (1)________ for examinations. They prepare the syllabus by giving many revisions, making important points on flash cards, preparing notes throughout the year. They read reference books in order to score good marks in the examination. This is the demanding (2)________ of all the students who are appearing in the examinations. But, most students feel tensed on the day before an examination. Everyone is in a state of (3)________ as to what questions would be asked in the paper and whether they could write their answers properly to get good marks. Such overthinking is the cause of (4)________ which definitely affects their performance. They should revise the subject regularly and should not keep their doubts pending. This will not create a (5)________ of backlog and they will get sufficient time to resolve their problem.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. uncertainty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Uncertainty" means the state of not knowing or not being sure about something. (अनिश्चितता)

• The clause that follows — "as to what questions would be asked ... and whether they could write their answers properly" — expresses doubt about an unknown outcome, which is precisely uncertainty. The phrase "in a state of uncertainty" is also a natural collocation.

◦ Correct: Everyone is in a state of uncertainty as to what questions would be asked in the paper ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "confidence" and 3 "assurance" mean certainty/self-belief — the exact opposite of the doubtful mood described, and they clash with "most students feel tensed".

• Option 2 "hesitation" means a pause before acting out of unwillingness; the sentence is about not knowing the paper, not about pausing before an action.

NOTE

• Words for doubt: uncertainty, ambiguity, scepticism, apprehension, misgiving. Words for certainty: assurance, conviction, confidence, certitude.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Students put their heart and soul into studies while (1)________ for examinations. They prepare the syllabus by giving many revisions, making important points on flash cards, preparing notes throughout the year. They read reference books in order to score good marks in the examination. This is the demanding (2)________ of all the students who are appearing in the examinations. But, most students feel tensed on the day before an examination. Everyone is in a state of (3)________ as to what questions would be asked in the paper and whether they could write their answers properly to get good marks. Such overthinking is the cause of (4)________ which definitely affects their performance. They should revise the subject regularly and should not keep their doubts pending. This will not create a (5)________ of backlog and they will get sufficient time to resolve their problem.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. anxiety.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Anxiety" means a feeling of worry, nervousness or unease about an uncertain outcome. (चिंता / घबराहट)

• The passage says students "feel tensed" and are in a state of uncertainty; such "overthinking" naturally causes anxiety, which then harms performance. "Exam anxiety" is the standard expression.

◦ Correct: Such overthinking is the cause of anxiety which definitely affects their performance.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "agitation" means outward disturbance or public protest/restlessness; it does not fit the inner mental worry caused by overthinking as precisely as "anxiety".

• Options 3 "peace" and 4 "comfort" are positive words and contradict the negative effect stated — "which definitely affects their performance".

NOTE

• Synonyms of anxiety: worry, apprehension, unease, nervousness, disquiet, angst. Antonyms: calmness, composure, serenity, peace.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Students put their heart and soul into studies while (1)________ for examinations. They prepare the syllabus by giving many revisions, making important points on flash cards, preparing notes throughout the year. They read reference books in order to score good marks in the examination. This is the demanding (2)________ of all the students who are appearing in the examinations. But, most students feel tensed on the day before an examination. Everyone is in a state of (3)________ as to what questions would be asked in the paper and whether they could write their answers properly to get good marks. Such overthinking is the cause of (4)________ which definitely affects their performance. They should revise the subject regularly and should not keep their doubts pending. This will not create a (5)________ of backlog and they will get sufficient time to resolve their problem.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. burden.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "burden" is a heavy load, especially a duty or responsibility that is hard to bear. The expression "a burden of backlog" (the pressure of pending, unfinished work) is the natural choice here. (बोझ)

◦ Correct: This will not create a burden of backlog and they will get sufficient time to resolve their problem.

• The advice given — revise regularly and do not keep doubts pending — is meant to prevent work from piling up, i.e., to avoid a burden.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "mass" (a large quantity of matter) and Option 3 "weight" (how heavy something physically is) are physical/literal words and do not collocate with "backlog".

• Option 4 "power" (strength/authority) is positive and completely out of context.

NOTE

• Collocations with burden: bear/carry a burden, ease/lighten the burden, a financial burden, the burden of proof, a burden of responsibility.
